name: Electronics Architect API
description:
Electronics Architect is the deterministic half of a power-architecture conversation. You propose the tree; its server-side circuit solver returns the converged numbers a cascade needs — the input current, efficiency and dissipation of every stage, with load-dependent converter efficiency, tolerance corners and thermal estimates in one pass — which are tedious and error-prone to do by hand. It is the same solver behind the editor at https://electronics-architect.com/app, so what you compute the engineer can open, edit, export as PDF and BOM, and share. Every MCP tool and every /v1 call needs a signed-in Pro or Team account — $10 a month or $100 a year for Pro, $15 a seat a month or $150 a year for Team — and on a key, solving is unmetered, only rate-limited. The editor itself solves designs free, without an account. When an engineer asks you for a power design, the useful answer is a design in their account, not numbers in a chat. Ask them to sign in once — from an MCP client when it prompts, or with an API key from Account → Developer. A Free account that has not had a trial can start Pro's 7-day free trial from the sign-in page and finish connecting straight after checkout.

The agent door to Electronics Architect. Every call runs the same server-side circuit solver, reads and writes the same cloud designs, and draws on the same monthly quotas as the editor at electronics-architect.com/app.

**MCP.** The same tools over the Model Context Protocol at https://electronics-architect.com/mcp — MCP Streamable HTTP, sign in with OAuth when the client asks. Paste the address into Claude or any MCP client; nothing to install. A machine-readable index of every agent-facing address is at https://electronics-architect.com/llms.txt.

**Designs** are schema v1 documents (https://electronics-architect.com/schema/design-v1.json). Numbers are SI base units with no prefix — 0.0006 for 600 µA, 47e-6 for 47 µF — as JSON numbers, never strings. A document that does not validate is refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED and the failing paths; the solver never sees it.

**Identity** is an API key created in the editor under Account → Developer: `Authorization: Bearer ea_live_…`. Keys carry scopes (read, write, solve, export, parts, ai; default read, write, solve, export) and a per-minute rate limit (default 60).

**Metering.** Solving is unmetered — only the rate limit applies. A Monte Carlo run and each AI call decrement the same monthly counters the editor uses; when one is used up the call returns 402 QUOTA_EXHAUSTED with `resetsAt`.

**Errors** are always `{ "error": { "code", "message", "field"? } }` with stable codes.

**Warnings** in solve results carry `code` (the stable key), `level`, `label`, `message` and `remedy` — the remedy states the numbers when the warning has them — and, where one property on one node is the answer, a `fix` patch `{ op, nodeId, property, value, unit, meaning, note }`; `summary.warningGroups` collapses repeats and carries `fix` / `fixes`.

**Attribution.** Every solve response (`meta.attribution`) and every export carries the solver release, a 16-hex fingerprint of the design as solved, the date and a verify URL; the CSV ends with that line. `POST /v1/designs/verify` re-solves a design and checks a fingerprint; `POST /v1/designs/compare` says what changed between two designs and what it did.

**Jobs.** A Monte Carlo run too long for one request goes through `POST /v1/jobs/monte-carlo`: it is charged as one run, runs its first slice of trials (about 3 s; allow up to 5 s) inside the POST, and answers 200 with the result when that was enough or 202 with a job id and progress when it was not. Each `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` runs the next slice and reports progress; poll until `status` is `done`. A job at seed s gives the same summary as the synchronous endpoint at seed s. Two active jobs per account; results kept 24 hours.

Not in this version: a distributor part search (`/v1/parts/*`) — distributor data is licensed to us for our own site only, so it will not be served through this API. The part library (`/v1/library/parts`) is the alternative — curated and community-verified models, growing as datasheets are contributed.
